## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

The *Kāsumāriphaladāyakattheraapadāna* is a canonical verse text preserved in the *Therāpadāna* section of the Pali Khuddaka Nikāya [SuttaCentral]. Like many biographical poems in this collection, it commemorates the meritorious past deed of a senior monk—specifically the offering of a *kāsumārī* fruit—and recounts the karmic fruits of that offering across subsequent rebirths. The text has been rendered into modern languages, with SuttaCentral cataloging five translations across five languages [SuttaCentral].

Computational analysis via DharmaNexus identifies 119 instances of internal text reuse shared across 43 other Pali texts, while no cross-language matches meet the threshold score [DharmaNexus]. Its largest external textual relationship is with the *Theragāthā-aṭṭhakathā*, where segments 1.1–4.1 align closely with the commentary [DharmaNexus]. Within the *Therāpadāna* itself, the poem exhibits near-verbatim formulaic parallels with other fruit-donation verses, most remarkably the nearly identical *Kāsumāraphaliyattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 505, segments 0.3–8.1 with 0.93 similarity), as well as the *Piyālaphaladāyakattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 502), *Labujaphaladāyakattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 469), and *Vallikāraphaladāyakattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 480) [DharmaNexus].

*No discussion of this text was found in the reference-literature corpus; the overview relies on SuttaCentral and DharmaNexus data.*
